question: If two resistors are connected in series, then which of the following statements is correct regarding the equivalent resistance of the circuit?

options.text: It will increase at first and then will decrease.

solution:
The correct answer is __**It will increase**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In a **series connection**, electrical components or **resistors** are joined end-to-end in a single path, meaning the **current** has only one route to flow through the circuit.
 
• The **equivalent resistance** (also known as total resistance) of resistors connected in series is calculated by the **arithmetic sum** of the individual resistances. The formula is expressed as **R_total = R1 + R2 + ... + Rn**.
 
• When a second resistor is added in series to an existing one, the total **opposition** to the flow of electric charge is **increased**. Consequently, the **equivalent resistance** of the circuit **will increase**. ***Hence, the statement that it will increase is correct.***
 
• In a series circuit, the **current** remains **constant** at every point in the loop, while the total **voltage** provided by the source is distributed
